text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Tuesday that Macquarie Bank Ltd (MBL) executive director Simon Hannes had been charged with one count of insider trading over trade in TNT Ltd options in September last year.
"On the information presently available to the ASC, the ASC holds no suspicion that anyone else from MBL is involved in any of the matters alleged against Mr Hannes," the ASC said in a statement.
"The prompt completion of this part of the ASC's investigation was assisted by co-operation from Macquarie," the ASC said.
"It is alleged that Mr Hannes had possession of price sensitive information about the takeover at the time he purchased, or procured the purchase of A$2 November 1996 TNT call options."
The ASC said the matter had been stood over until June 10.
The charge arose from investigations into transactions in TNT call options before the successful A$2.45 a share takeover bid by Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).

The ASC laid charges of not reporting financial transations against Hannes on January 20, but stopped short of full insider trading charges. Hannes has pleaded not guilty to those transactions reporting charges.
Macquarie Bank was the adviser to TNT Ltd on the eventually successful takeover bid for the transport group by the Dutch telecommunications and postal group, KPN.
Hannes is a senior executive of the bank's corporate advisory division, but was not part of the team working on the TNT transaction, Macquarie said in January.
Hannes had been on extended leave at the time of the TNT bid, but was available for part-time consultation.
Hannes was named in court in February as the fictitious TNT options trader Mark Booth, who made a A$2 million profit after buying about A$90,000 of the TNT options.
Hannes was alleged to have withdrawn sums of A$9,900 or less from his bank accounts and then paid them into an account in the name of M. Booth.
A financial transaction must be reported under the Financial Transactions Reports Act if above A$10,000.
Hannes was charged with trying to avoid reporting the transaction.
TNT's shares were trading around A$1.60 at the time of the A$2.45 bid.
